events.title: Council of Trent Opens
events.description: Pope Paul III's Council of Trent convened in northern Italy, beginning a series of sessions that would last until 1563 and define Catholic doctrine and reforms.
events.significance: The council was the centerpiece of the Counter-Reformation, clarifying Catholic teaching in response to Protestantism and shaping the Church for roughly four centuries.

events.title: Francis Drake Departs on Circumnavigation
events.description: Sir Francis Drake set sail from Plymouth, England, with five ships on an expedition that would become the second circumnavigation of the globe.
events.significance: The voyage, completed in 1580, brought Drake fame and wealth, challenged Spanish dominance in the Pacific, and boosted English maritime ambitions.

events.title: Abel Tasman Sights New Zealand
events.description: Dutch explorer Abel Tasman, sailing for the Dutch East India Company, became the first European to sight New Zealand's South Island.
events.significance: The sighting placed New Zealand on European maps, though sustained European contact did not begin until Captain James Cook's voyages over a century later.

events.title: Nanjing Massacre Begins
events.description: Japanese forces captured the Chinese capital of Nanjing and began weeks of mass killings, rapes, and destruction of civilians and prisoners of war.
events.significance: One of the worst atrocities of World War II in Asia, it remains a deeply significant and contested issue in China-Japan relations and a symbol of wartime brutality.

events.title: Saddam Hussein Captured
events.description: Former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein was captured by U.S. forces near Tikrit, Iraq, in Operation Red Dawn, hiding in a small underground hole at a farmhouse.
events.significance: His capture ended a manhunt after the 2003 invasion of Iraq and led to his trial and execution in 2006, marking a pivotal moment in the Iraq War.
